title: Utility Upgrades, Voter Drive, Anti-Apartheid Stance
summary:
*   **Electric Utility's Anti-Apartheid Stance**: Recommended against further changes to the city's anti-apartheid ordinance due to concerns about securing essential parts for the power system.
*   **Voter Registration Drive**: Approved a plan to include voter registration cards with upcoming utility bills to encourage greater civic participation.
*   **Major Power Infrastructure Investments**: Authorized over $17 million in contracts for critical electric utility equipment, including substation transformers, power plant security gates, and natural gas supplies for electricity generation.

Mayor Cooke called to order the meeting of the Council, meeting as the Electric Utility

Robert Floyd, Chairman, Electric Utility Commission, presented the report of the
Commission. He said they recommended no further amendments to the Anti-Apartheid Ordinance
because technical difficulties could result for the Electric Department regarding purchase
of needed parts for upkeep of the City's electrical system. Mr. Floyd said the Commission
also recommends including voter registration cards in the next billing cycle.
There was no report given by the Resource Management Commission.
